newsitem.title: UK: UK's Flextech cuts losses in current year.
newsitem.headline: UK's Flextech cuts losses in current year.

text.p: Flextech Plc, the British television programming subsidiary of the U.S.-based Tele-Communications International Inc said on Friday it had reduced its losses in the six-month period to June 30, 1997.

The company said its operation of restructuring its associated channel investments combined with repositioning of its existing channel portfolio helped it to raise its turnover by 80 percent to 44.6 million stg.
The company's operating losses before exceptional items fell to 4.7 million stg from 8.5 million stg in 1996.
Flextech operates a variety of cable and satellite channels in the UK including UK Gold, Bravo TV, Playboy TV, Trouble, Family Channel and Challenge TV.

Flextech recently completed two joint ventures with the British Broadcasting Corporation. The first will develop and launch up to eight new basic subscription channels while the second will develop UK Gold.
Flextech said its viewing share in basic cable and satellite television currently stood at 25 percent.
Nearly 26 percent of British multi-channel households are currently wired up to basic cable and satellite channels.
The company incurred exceptional costs of five million stg in launching Trouble and repositioning Bravo. The company spent another 1.6 million stg in launching Challenge TV.
Flextech's subscription revenue rose 67 percent to 22.4 million stg while advertising revenue more than doubled to five million.
Revenue from home shopping business rose to eight million stg from 4.6 million.

"As a result of or strategy of taking control of our associated channel investments, we have succeeded in repositioning our channel portfolio to attract a broad range of advertisers and viewers," the company said.
"Flextech is confident that its programming and channel position leave it well placed for the balance of 1997 and the future," it added.
